articles.title: Fingerhut On Schmidt Cameras At August Meeting
articles.summary: Bob Fingerhut will present on the art of Schmidt camera photography at the general meeting on Saturday, August 16, at Houge Park. He will showcase his 5-inch Schmidt camera, describe its operation and usage, share his widefield images from both northern and southern skies, and provide technical literature. This event promises a fascinating introduction to unique photographic techniques from a highly skilled SJAA member.

articles.title: New SJAA EMail List and Forum
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) has launched a new subscription email list and forum, initiated by Bill Arnett with support from SEDS. This platform will distribute the monthly Ephemeris, provide timely event notifications, and facilitate discussions on club-related ideas and issues. Members can subscribe by sending an email with the word "subscribe" to sjaa-request@seds.org.

articles.title: SJAA Activities Calendar
articles.summary: This document outlines the San Jose Astronomical Association's (SJAA) activities calendar for August and September, detailing various club events. It lists multiple star parties at locations like Henry Coe, Fremont Peak, and Houge Park, often noting moon conditions and sunset times. The calendar also includes general meetings with guest speakers on topics like Schmidt Camera Photography and Slide & Equipment Night, alongside beginning astronomy classes covering chart software and CCD astronomy.

articles.title: SJAA Invades Yosemite
articles.summary: The article recounts an SJAA public event held on June 27-28 in Yosemite, detailing the author's drive, camping at Bridalveil Creek, and setting up telescopes at Glacier Point. The event involved daytime terrestrial viewing of park features, preparations for astrophotography, and engaging the public with around 15 telescopes and 25 SJAA members present.

articles.title: Bill Arnett
articles.summary: The author recounts a highly successful astronomical observing weekend at Lassen, primarily at Devastated Area and Bumpass Hell. They describe exceptional dark skies, allowing for clear views of the Milky Way, numerous deep-sky objects like the Crescent and Omega Nebulae, and the moons of Uranus and Saturn. Despite some varied seeing conditions, the experience was profoundly positive, highlighting the beauty of the night sky and the camaraderie with fellow astronomers.

articles.title: Bill Dellinges
articles.summary: The author attended the Grand Canyon Starparty (GCSP) on the South Rim for two nights in June, participating in public stargazing despite challenging windy conditions at 7000 feet elevation. The event featured around fifteen telescopes, attracting hundreds of visitors each night, and provided opportunities for sharing observations and camaraderie among amateur astronomers. Key observations included white clouds on Mars through a 9-inch refractor and deep-sky objects like NGC 6888 and NGC 7789, showcasing the value of filters and computer-aided navigation for celestial viewing.

articles.title: Ups And Downs Of Mountains (or Testing A New Lightning Rod)
articles.summary: After being disappointed with viewing conditions at Fremont Peak, the author relocated to the Sierra Nevada, where he experienced exceptionally transparent skies, observing 7th magnitude stars naked eye and enjoying spectacular views of the Milky Way and deep-sky objects. His observing session was briefly interrupted by a close lightning storm, necessitating a rapid pack-up of expensive equipment. Despite the disruption, he resumed his activities, capturing several fantastic photographic images and witnessing a bright meteor.

articles.title: What Children Should Know
articles.summary: This article by Bill Arnett outlines fundamental astronomical concepts children should learn, covering topics like the solar system's structure, Earth's movements, the nature of stars, and the immense scale of the universe. It encourages making these abstract ideas concrete through practical activities like sky watching with an astronomy club and teaching astronomy's historical development. The piece emphasizes nurturing an understanding of the universe's vastness.

articles.title: Yosemite, continued from page 1
articles.summary: This article details two nights of extensive astronomical observing at Yosemite, emphasizing the exceptional dark and transparent skies. The observer, utilizing various telescopes and binoculars, reported views of numerous celestial objects including planets (Mars, Jupiter), nebulae (e.g., Trifid, Veil, North American), star clusters, and galaxies (e.g., Andromeda, NGC 7331). The narrative highlights the beauty of the summer Milky Way and shared observing experiences with fellow astronomers and public visitors.

articles.title: Theophilus, Cyrillus and Half Dome
articles.summary: The article describes observing the prominent lunar craters Theophilus and Cyrillus during a Santa Cruz Yosemite Star Party, detailing their physical features, historical interpretations, and comparing them to Yosemite's Half Dome. It also covers the changing views of these craters over successive nights as the lunar terminator moves, and briefly mentions a separate deep-sky observing session for faint fuzzy objects.

articles.title: Class Notes
articles.summary: The 'Class Notes' recap highlights a successful July Beginning Astronomy Class featuring a moon presentation and lunar observing, which, despite an initial police call, concluded positively with officers joining the viewing. The article also previews upcoming classes, including 'Charts and Software' in August and a 'CCDs' introduction by Kevin Medlock in September, emphasizing their importance for beginners and advanced topics.

articles.title: Walden West Star Party
articles.summary: The SJAA is hosting a star party on the evening of August 9th at Walden West School, serving as a fundraiser benefit for the school. Attendees are encouraged to arrive early, with free food also mentioned, and detailed directions to the location are provided.

articles.title: The Far Side Of The Moon
articles.summary: On June 20, 1997, a favorable libration allowed the author to observe Mare Orientale, normally on the Moon's far side, from Los Altos, CA, using a 6" Cave telescope. The report details the lunar feature's profile, including its concentric mountain ranges, and notes a brief interlude to observe an occultation of Jupiter's moons Europa and Ganymede. The author also made a sketch of previously unnoticed craters near Orientale, highlighting the rarity of such observations.

articles.title: Exploring The August 12 Perseid Outburst
articles.summary: This article details an anticipated Perseid meteor outburst on August 12, 1997, expected to be a significant event for observers on the West Coast, particularly in the San Francisco Bay Area. A NASA-funded project at Ames Research Center is organizing an observing campaign utilizing photographic cameras at multiple sites and actively recruiting volunteer visual observers to help triangulate meteor trajectories. Training sessions are planned, and individuals can also contribute remotely from their own locations.

articles.title: Table 1: 1997 Perseid Outburst Predicted Rates
articles.summary: This document, titled "Table 1: 1997 Perseid Outburst Predicted Rates," provides a detailed forecast of observing conditions for the Perseid meteor shower outburst on August 11th/12th, 1997. It lists hourly predictions for various parameters including solar longitude, Universal Time, radiant and moon altitudes, and Zenith Hourly Rates, specifically tailored for observers in California. The table also indicates the expected percentage of meteors contributing to the outburst, with a clear peak identified.

articles.title: Board Meeting Notes
articles.summary: The board discussed the club's financial health, noting it's under budget despite a slight dip in membership. Operational changes are being implemented for the Ephemeris publication and mailing list, and new events were added to the schedule. Discussions with Fremont Peak Park ranger Rick Morales focused on dark sky issues, potential park improvements, and the success of dark sky ordinances in Salinas.

articles.title: Directions to SJAA places
articles.summary: This document provides detailed driving directions to several parks in the San Jose, California area and beyond, specifically identifying them as 'SJAA places' or sites used by related astronomical groups. It includes instructions for reaching Houge Park, Henry Coe State Park, Fremont Peak State Park, and Grant Ranch County Park, noting entrance fees and associations with star parties. The document is dated August 1997 and is part of an 'SJAA EPHEMERIS'.

articles.title: Celestial Calendar - June 1997
articles.summary: This June 1997 celestial calendar update reports on the recent discovery of Comet Tabur (C/1997 N1) in the southern sky, which will become visible to Northern Hemisphere observers in a few months. It also notes the continued dimming of Comet Hale-Bopp and SOHO satellite's detection of five new Kreutz Sungrazing comets. The article highlights trends in visual comet discoveries, predominantly occurring in the southern morning sky.

articles.title: Ephemerides -- Epoch 2000, 0h UTC
articles.summary: This document provides ephemerides for two comets, C/1995 O1 (Hale-Bopp) and C/1997 N1 (Tabur), for dates ranging from August 5th to September 9th. For each comet, it lists celestial coordinates (Right Ascension and Declination), elongation from the Sun or Moon ('EL Sky'), and visual magnitude, all referenced to Epoch 2000, 0h UTC.

articles.title: Orbital Elements -- Epoch 2000.0
articles.summary: This document provides detailed orbital elements for two comets, Hale-Bopp and Tabur, referenced to Epoch 2000.0. It lists parameters such as perihelion date and distance, argument of perihelion, ascending node, inclination, eccentricity, and estimated orbital periods, along with their respective absolute magnitudes and data references. The information is presented in a tabular format for easy comparison of the celestial objects.

It serves as a guide for locating and observing Mercury during the specified period.

It lists key observational data, including two daily times (possibly rise/set or visibility windows), transit times, apparent magnitude (around -4.4), and celestial coordinates (Right Ascension and Declination). This information is suitable for planning observations or tracking Venus's position in the sky.

articles.title: SOL Star Type G2V Intelligent Life in System ?
articles.summary: The document presents a table of astronomical data, including rise, transit, and set times, along with celestial coordinates (Right Ascension and a declination-like value) for specific dates. The accompanying title, "SOL Star Type G2V Intelligent Life in System ?", poses a provocative question about the existence of intelligent life within our solar system, framing the provided ephemeris-like data within a broader philosophical context.

articles.title: Astronomical Twilight
articles.summary: This document presents a table detailing the begin and end times of astronomical twilight for specific dates, referenced by Julian Date. It provides practical time-based data for various days. This information is essential for astronomers to plan observations, as astronomical twilight signifies the period when the sky is sufficiently dark for most astronomical viewing.

It includes entries for 'Transit Night,' 'Ascension at,' and 'Local Midnite,' each with a corresponding numerical value and a time conversion (e.g., 00:00=19:55). This information likely pertains to astronomical observations or timekeeping.

articles.summary: This document outlines a schedule of astronomical events for August, primarily featuring star parties and lunar observing sessions. These public and member events are hosted by various astronomy clubs such as TAC, PAS, HVAC, and HVAG at multiple locations throughout the month.

The schedule includes multiple opportunities for stargazing and lunar observation throughout the month.

articles.summary: This document provides a status update for a telescope loaner program, listing various telescopes along with their current borrowers, due dates, or availability. articles.title: Submit
articles.summary: The SJAA Ephemeris invites its members to submit articles for publication in the newsletter. Submissions should be emailed to Dave North at Timocharis@aol.com by the 10th of each month to be included in the following month's issue. Authors are required to include their name and phone number with their submission.

articles.title: Periodical Publication Statement
articles.summary: The SJAA Ephemeris, the official newsletter of the San Jose Astronomical Association, is published monthly, totaling 12 issues annually from January through December. The statement also provides the mailing address for the San Jose Astronomical Association.

articles.title: San Jose Astronomical Association Membership Form
articles.summary: This document is a membership form for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), detailing membership fees ($15 for regular, $6 for junior) and an optional Sky and Telescope magazine subscription for an additional $27. It provides instructions for submitting the form and payment via mail to the treasurer, Bob Eisberry, or in person at an SJAA meeting, along with contact details. The form was published in August 1997.
